item.title: Risk assessment of benzophenone-3, a UV filter in cosmetics
item.description: Benzophenone-3 (also known as oxybenzone) is an ultraviolet filter commonly used in sunscreen formulations and personal care products. Given its systemic exposure through dermal and oral absorption, the toxicity of benzophenone-3 has been widely studied. In rodents, dietary exposure to high experimental doses of benzophenone-3 was associated with mild systemic toxicity, including reduction in body weight gain, increase in liver and kidney weights, and signs of nephropathy. While benzophenone-3...

item.title: Expansion of Korea's Special Estimate Case System and changes in out-of-pocket expenditure: an interrupted time-series analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The implementation and expansion of the Special Estimate Case System were associated with reductions in the proportion of OOP expenditure, although the patterns differed by type of care and healthcare institution. After excluding medical expenditure for care covered under the system, OOP expenditure proportions were closer to the statutory copayment rates under the NHI. These findings may inform future policy discussions on the selection of eligible diseases and patient groups and...

item.title: Preventive administration of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis HEM20-01 attenuates the development of atopic dermatitis-like inflammation in mice, along with gut microbial and succinate alterations
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Preventive HEM20-01 administration attenuates the development of AD-like phenotypes and associated behavioral alterations, accompanied by changes in gut microbiome composition, lower circulating succinate, and intestinal inflammatory signaling.

item.title: Metal-Catalyzed Benzannulation: Recent Advances in Catalyst Design, Mechanistic Insights, and Aromatic Framework Construction
item.description: Benzannulation is a key transformation in organic synthesis, enabling direct access to aromatic and heteroaromatic scaffolds central to natural products, pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, dyes, electronic devices, and materials. The construction of these frameworks continues to pose a challenge because it requires high regioselectivity, broad substrate scope, and functional-group tolerance. Traditional multistep approaches often suffer from limited efficiency, highlighting the need for more...

item.title: Managing the Spatial Interactions of Ligands on Perovskite Quantum Dot Films for Efficient Photovoltaic Devices
item.description: Although perovskite quantum dot (PQD) photovoltaics have evolved swiftly, the stability of their devices still lags far behind that of their polycrystalline counterparts, which limits our understanding of how to modulate the spatial interactions of novel, highly stable ligands in PQD thin films to maximize their photophysical performance. Herein, using the fluorine-rich moiety pentafluorobenzyl as a template, O-(2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzyl)hydroxylammonium (5FBHA) as a post-synthetic ligand was...

item.title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto-Viscoelastic Patches
item.description: We report a machine learning (ML)-augmented magnetic sensing system for real-time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″-Fe(16)N(2) microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium...
item.category: IBS, KIST, Kyung Hee University, SNU

item.title: Korean Medication Algorithm Project for Bipolar Disorder 2026, Sixth Revision: An Executive Summary
item.description: CONCLUSION: The KMAP-BP 2026 reflects both the evolving landscape of psychiatric practice in Korea and the accumulation of recent pharmacotherapy evidence, reflecting both continuity and refinement of prior recommendations. These updated recommendations are intended to serve as a practical, evidence-informed resource for clinicians navigating the complexities of bipolar disorder management.

item.title: Real-world Longitudinal Patterns of Benzodiazepine Use in Korean Patients with First-onset Panic Disorder: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Long-term BZD use frequently persisted among BZD-initiating patients with first-onset panic disorder despite guideline recommendations for short-term adjunctive use. A substantial proportion of patients continue BZDs beyond 12 months in real-world clinical practice, indicating a clear gap between treatment guidelines and actual prescribing patterns.

item.title: Predicting Polysomnography‑derived Sleep Efficiency and Total Sleep Time Using Clinical Questionnaires: A Machine Learning Approach
item.description: CONCLUSION: Validated self-report instruments effectively captured clinically meaningful determinants of sleep efficiency and total sleep time. Machine learning models, particularly CatBoost, demonstrated robust performance using questionnaire-derived features alone, highlighting the central roles of age, insomnia severity, and daytime sleepiness. These findings support the feasibility and clinical utility of accessible, questionnaire-driven machine learning approaches for large-scale screening,...

item.title: The Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) and the Five Aggregates (skandha-s) of the Early Buddhism: Parallels and Differences on Understanding of Human Mind
item.description: The research domain criteria (RDoC) was launched by the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) to provide a framework towards development of neurobiological models and novel treatment methods for mental health disorders. Here we elucidate the possible parallels between the RDoC and the understanding of human mind by the early Buddhism, conceptualized as the five aggregates (skandha-s). They both define the function of human mind as a collective operation of de-centralized systems. The...

item.title: Digital Psychiatry with Physical Artificial Intelligence: Recent Advances and Limitations
item.description: Digital psychiatry has evolved from screen-based and virtual systems toward physically embodied artificial intelligence (AI) capable of perceiving and acting in the real world. Physical AI integrates sensors, cognitive algorithms, and actuators into closed perception-cognition-action loops, enabling dynamic and multimodal interaction with patients. This narrative review synthesizes recent advances in the technological foundations, clinical applications, and ethical implications of physical AI...

item.title: Two-injection Start Strategy of Aripiprazole Once-monthly Injection: Current Evidence and Clinical Implications
item.description: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics (LAIs) are developed to overcome the limitations of oral antipsychotics (APs) and their use has been increasing in the treatment of various psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. LAIs are convenient to use and they were also found to enhance treatment adherence and continuation, leading to better clinical outcomes. Aripiprazole (ARP), a partial D2/5-HT1A receptor agonist, has been considered to have fewer adverse events than...

item.title: Pharmacologic Treatment Response in Panic Disorder with Comorbid Medical Conditions: A Systematic and Narrative Review
item.description: Panic disorder frequently co-occurs with medical conditions, complicating diagnosis and treatment. Although pharmacotherapy is a first-line treatment for panic disorder, pharmacotherapeutic evidence for patients with medical comorbidities is limited. Therefore, this review systematically evaluates the efficacy of pharmacologic treatments for panic disorder in adults with medical comorbidities and synthesizes clinical insights using a narrative approach. We searched PubMed, Embase, and the...

item.title: Impact of material type and acidic oral environment on physical properties and protein adsorption of subtractively and additively manufactured resin-ceramics for definitive crowns
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although the roughness of tested materials remained below clinical thresholds, acidic aging increased surface irregularities and reduced the hardness. VE may be more resistant to wear and protein accumulation-related complications than PC with acidic oral challenges.

item.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Energy Devices for Thyroidectomy: An Outcome-Specific Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Harmonic showed the most favorable relative effects across the evaluated outcomes. However, these findings do not establish overall device superiority; selection should consider absolute benefits and device-specific characteristics.

item.title: Functional Characterization and Application of Yarrowia lipolytica YlYxc1 for Enhanced Production of Sphingoid Bases
item.description: Long-chain bases (LCBs; sphingoid bases), derived from ceramide metabolism, are valuable sphingolipid intermediates for industrial applications. Here, we functionally characterized a putative ceramidase from Yarrowia lipolytica (YlYxc1) and evaluated its potential to enhance LCB production. YlYxc1 contains a conserved alkaline ceramidase motif with seven transmembrane helices and shares ~42% amino acid identity with Saccharomyces cerevisiae alkaline ceramidases ScYpc1 and ScYdc1. Despite lacking...

item.title: Comparative Evaluation of Synthetic and Xenogeneic Self-Retaining Bone Grafting Systems Under Standardized Block Geometry: An Experimental In Vivo Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The synthetic self-retaining grafting system showed greater new bone formation than the xenogeneic system after 8 weeks of healing in this canine model.

item.title: Response to: 'Confounded Prosthetic Interfaces and Statistical Inconsistency in Zirconia vs. PFM Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Outcomes'
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Multi-periodic photonic mechanism for non-spectral magenta coloration in Anna's hummingbird (Calypte anna) feathers
item.description: Hummingbird feathers generate iridescent colours through light interference within multi-layered arrays of platelet-shaped melanosomes embedded in corneous beta-protein. In Anna's hummingbird (Calypte anna), the gorget feathers produce a non-spectral magenta hue with multiple reflectance peaks in the red and blue spectral regions. The primary red peak has been attributed to the melanosome stack; however, the optical mechanism underlying the secondary blue peak remains unexplained. Here, we...

item.title: Age-Related Differences in Decision-Making Roles and End-of-Life Care Trajectories Among Adults With Cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although older adults were referred earlier to palliative care, they were less likely to make their own treatment decisions, and aggressive care remained common. These findings indicate a need for age-sensitive approaches to improve end-of-life care.

item.title: Human nasal organoids sustain reproducible airway epithelial differentiation and influenza virus-host innate immune interaction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study's results demonstrate that human NEC organoids serve as a robust in vitro model, successfully recapitulating the biological characteristics of nasal epithelium, and could be an adequate tool for exploring distinct IFN-related innate immune responses following influenza infection.

item.title: Working alone and depressive mood among Korean employees: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study found that working alone was significantly associated with depressive mood among Korean employees. These findings suggest that working alone should be considered an important workplace factor in efforts to promote workers' mental health.

item.title: Cancer therapy resistance converges on immune evasion: a unified framework from immunotherapy to targeted, endocrine, and DNA repair pathways
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: By reframing resistance as a new immune state that converges on the same three immune-evasion axes rather than a terminal event, this review shifts attention from why a therapy failed to which immune-evasion axis now predominates and how it might be countered. This perspective supports mechanism-matched combination therapy, adaptive molecular monitoring, and cautious exploitation of vulnerabilities generated by the resistant state itself. As an organizing model rather than a claim...

item.title: Prognostic implications of the duration of continuous kidney replacement therapy in 3-month survivors of acute kidney injury: findings from the LINKA cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged CKRT was independently associated with an increased risk of long-term ESKD progression and all-cause mortality among 3-month survivors of AKI. Thus, the duration of CKRT may serve as a meaningful prognostic marker to identify high-risk patients who might benefit from close follow-up and tailored multidisciplinary management.

item.title: A House Divided: Unifying the Classification of Plant Pathogen Effectors
item.description: Plant pathogens deploy diverse effectors to interfere with host defense systems and create favorable conditions for infection. As effector biology has advanced, the terminology used to describe these effectors has become increasingly complex, reflecting differences in secretion pathways, molecular features, and subcellular localization across pathogens. This inconsistency complicates comparative studies and limits effective communication across research groups. Here, we propose a streamlined and...

item.title: Preoperative Inflammatory Ratios Poorly Discriminate Malignant From Benign Parotid Tumours
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although the two primary ratios were higher in malignant tumours, their distributions overlapped substantially and discrimination was poor. These findings do not support their use as stand-alone markers for preoperative malignancy risk stratification.

item.title: Comparison of rebleeding risk after navigation-guided catheterization and thrombolytic irrigation using tPA or urokinase in intracerebral hemorrhage
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In catheter-based minimally invasive treatment of spontaneous supratentorial ICH, urokinase was associated with a lower risk of rebleeding and more favorable early neurological outcomes than tPA, despite comparable mean hematoma reduction.

item.title: Designing a tumor landscape-modifying vaccine with a unique TLR2/6 agonist for refractory pancreatic cancer
item.description: Failure of cancer vaccines in clinical trials has been linked to poor preclinical translatability, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments (TMEs), suboptimal antigen delivery to antigen-presenting cells, limited human MHC antigenicity, and insufficiently safe immune adjuvants. Therefore, this study aimed to design an integrated cancer vaccine and evaluate its efficacy in a KPC orthotopic pancreatic cancer model containing the G12D mutation. A novel immune adjuvant, C-VAX, was developed from...

item.title: Serum albumin maintains Wnt3a water solubility and activity
item.description: Wnt proteins regulate adult tissue homeostasis and repair by driving stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. High-performance Wnt preparations have enormous therapeutic potential, especially alongside various stem cell technologies. Currently, a major limitation of most Wnt preparations is that they inevitably require fetal bovine serum (FBS) or detergents to maintain Wnt solubility and activity. Recently, afamin (AFM) was identified as a serum factor that solubilizes Wnt3a in conditioned...

item.title: Metal cofactor-level chassis engineering enables aerobic expression of tungsten formate dehydrogenases in Escherichia coli
item.description: Tungsten-dependent formate dehydrogenases are among the most active biological catalysts for carbon dioxide reduction, but their production is limited by complex metal cofactor requirements and poor compatibility with standard expression hosts. Here, we address this limitation by engineering an Escherichia coli chassis through reconstruction of tungsten cofactor biosynthesis, installation of a high-affinity tungstate transporter, and reinforcement of iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis. The resulting...

item.title: Intraskeletal Pathway of the Trigeminal Nerve in Modern Bird Beak: 3D Comparative Anatomy Using the diceCT Method
item.description: The morphology of the trigeminal nerve extending through the snout region in Archosauria has recently been the focus of extensive research, particularly in paleontology. However, the pathways of this nerve within cranial bones in extant birds have not been described in detail. Here, we describe trigeminal nerve pathways in the skull of nine avian species using a non-destructive soft-tissue imaging technique (diceCT) with a particular emphasis on osteological correlates, including intraskeletal...

item.title: Age-Specific Effectiveness of Antiviral Agents on the Secondary Household Transmission of Influenza
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight that both clinical and demographic factors substantially influence household influenza transmission. Early initiation of antiviral treatment, combined with the use of Baloxavir or Laninamivir, significantly reduces the risk of secondary transmission, particularly in younger populations who play a central role in household spread.

item.title: Constant versus seasonal photoperiod and temperature yield divergent life-history responses to climate warming
item.description: A key goal of predictive ecology is to understand how global warming affects ectotherm growth and development. Researchers often rear organisms under constant temperature and photoperiod regimes, raising the question of whether responses under these simplified conditions reflect those in realistic, seasonally varying environments. We examined key life-history traits of the damselfly Lestes sponsa across six combinations of constant and seasonal temperatures and photoperiod regimes, simulating...

item.title: Development and temporal validation of a screening-based prediction model for suicidal ideation at first contact with university counseling services
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Routinely collected mental health screening data can predict suicidal ideation at the time of initial counseling contact with reasonable accuracy and potential clinical utility. Screening‑based prediction models may strengthen existing student support systems by enabling earlier identification of elevated risk and guiding proportionate intervention strategies.

item.title: Genotypic and clinical characteristics of long-term surviving adult patients with urea cycle disorders in Japan
item.description: CONCLUSION: This is the first study to characterize the genetic and clinical profiles of adult long-term survivors with UCDs in Japan. These findings suggest that genotype information may help predict disease onset and clinical severity, although genotype alone is insufficient to fully predict long-term clinical outcomes.

item.title: Predicting olanzapine induced BMI increase using machine learning on population-based electronic health records
item.description: CONCLUSION: Routinely collected electronic health record data predicted olanzapine-associated BMI increase with moderate discrimination, but performance was less stable in temporally held-out data. The model associations were consistent with known risk patterns for olanzapine-associated weight gain and highlighted less established predictors of BMI increase during olanzapine treatment. These findings may support future work on risk stratification and metabolic monitoring, but they should be...

item.title: Characterization of etoposide-resistant choriocarcinoma cells and contribution of MAPK7 to etoposide resistance
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that the MAPK signaling pathway, particularly MAPK7, contributes to etoposide resistance in choriocarcinoma, based on RNA sequencing and functional analyses of resistant cell models.

item.title: Association of COVID-19 infection with welfare recipients in Japan: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The diagnosed/confirmed COVID-19 infection was associated with an increased likelihood of receiving public assistance. Furthermore, individuals who had not utilized hospital or clinic services in 2019 were at the highest risk of becoming welfare recipients compared with other individuals.

item.title: Colorimetric Microplate Assay Coupled with Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling for High-Throughput Evaluation of Ophthalmic Preservatives
item.description: Conventional preservative efficacy tests for ophthalmic formulations rely on discrete colony counts and therefore provide limited insight into the dynamic processes of microbial inactivation and recovery. Such endpoint-based evaluations can obscure formulation-dependent differences in antimicrobial performance and hinder rational optimization of preservative systems. In this study, we developed a quantitative framework that integrates a high-throughput WST-8-based colorimetric microplate assay...

item.title: Molecular characterization of a myxoepithelioid tumor with chordoid features: aberrant hormone receptor expression and Wnt pathway activation in SMARCB1-deficient neoplasms
item.description: Myxoepithelioid tumor with chordoid features (METC) is a rare SMARCB1-deficient soft tissue neoplasm. In this study, we comprehensively investigated the molecular expression profile of 14 METC cases, comparing them with 13 proximal-type epithelioid sarcoma (ES) cases. Distinct molecular characteristics were exhibited by METC, including consistent androgen receptor (AR) and estrogen receptor expression, Hedgehog signaling suppression, and Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation. Moreover, gene...

item.title: Reply to Comments on "Nationwide trends in cardiac anesthesia requiring cardiopulmonary bypass and intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography use in Japan: a claims-based analysis, 2019-2023"
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Accuracy of CSF tap test and lumbar infusion test in predicting shunt response in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Both CSF-TT and LIT show poor specificity for predicting shunt responsiveness in iNPH, with low-certainty evidence for CSF-TT and moderate-certainty evidence for LIT. A positive result from either test should not be used in isolation to guide surgical decisions. Standardized prospective studies with clearly defined patient selection criteria and outcome measures are needed to establish the true diagnostic value of these tests.

item.title: Gut microbial immunometabolic pathways associated with cardiac arrest risk: genetic evidence and exploratory fecal microbiome profiling
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings prioritize an immunometabolic framework linking gut microbial variation to cardiac arrest risk, with metabolic mediation representing the predominant candidate layer for follow-up study. The exploratory clinical 16S results provide descriptive post-arrest context rather than independent validation, and the genetic findings should be interpreted as candidate associations requiring larger prospective and experimental confirmation.

item.title: Growth, nutritional status, and physical fitness trajectories among primary and secondary school students and their associations with poor vision: a school-based study in Chongqing, China
item.description: CONCLUSION: From 2022 to 2026, growth and development indicators among primary and secondary school students in Yuzhong District improved, while poor vision remained prevalent. BMI and VCI trajectories were associated with poor vision, highlighting the importance of integrated monitoring and targeted interventions.

item.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues
item.description: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an...

item.title: A posteriori error estimates for mixed-dimensional Darcy flow using non-matching grids
item.description: In this article, we extend the a posteriori error estimates for hierarchical mixed-dimensional elliptic equations developed in [Varela et al., J. Numer. Math., 31 (2023), pp. 247-280] to the setting of non-matching mixed-dimensional grids. The extension is achieved by introducing transfer grids between the planar subdomain and interface grids, together with stable discrete projection operators for primal (potential) and dual (flux) variables and grid mismatch operators. The proposed estimators...

item.title: A novel endoscopy-guided airway management strategy for lateral decubitus endoscopic procedures
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this feasibility cohort, gastrointestinal endoscopy-guided endotracheal intubation demonstrated a 100% first-attempt success rate with a mean intubation time of 30.95 ± 6.58 s and no severe complications. These preliminary findings suggest that the technique appears to be a feasible and safe option for airway management in patients undergoing lateral-position gastrointestinal endoscopy. However, these findings are from an uncontrolled, single-center study with a limited sample...

item.title: Gut microbiome taxonomic and functional capacity alterations in CHD and HFpEF
item.description: The gut microbiome is known to modulate metabolic health, yet its role in coronary heart disease (CHD) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains unclear. In the present study, we profiled the gut microbiome of 234 participants using shotgun metagenomic sequencing across controls (n = 43), individuals with low-risk atherosclerosis (LRAS, n = 23), and patients with CHD + HFpEF (n = 168). Species richness was significantly increased in CHD + HFpEF, with no disruption in...

item.title: Knockout and re-expression system for mutant analysis in primary mouse T cells
item.description: We describe here an efficient method for gene editing in mouse T cells, based on well-established, high-efficiency retroviral transduction protocols. Our platform allows analysis of mutant phenotypes in primary murine T cells in vitro and in vivo. This approach uses a single retroviral vector to simultaneously knockout an endogenous gene and ectopically express its mutant version. This knockout/re-expression vector can be used as the only plasmid to transduce Cas9-expressing T cells, or used...

item.title: Human CD46 humanized mice reveal interferon associated pulmonary immune remodeling during human adenovirus type 7 lung infection
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: HAdV-7 infection in hCD46 humanized mice was associated with an interferon enriched pulmonary inflammatory environment, prominent inflammatory myeloid remodeling, and altered lymphoid transcriptional states. This susceptible mouse model provides a useful experimental tool for studying HAdV-7 associated lung disease and for preclinical evaluation of antiviral, immunomodulatory, and vaccine strategies.

item.title: Privacy-preserving synthetic data from a national CIDP registry: validation against real-world evidence
item.description: CONCLUSION: SD derived from the Italian CIDP Registry accurately reproduces key analytical properties of real-world data while preserving patient privacy. This approach enables reproducible and shareable CIDP research and may support future applications, including synthetic standard-of-care comparator cohorts and precision medicine-oriented investigations.

item.title: Social support and cognition in a racially and ethnically diverse cohort: the role of neighborhood disadvantage
item.description: CONCLUSION: Tangible Support, and to a lesser extent Emotional Support, showed positive associations with cognition across ethnoracial groups, with the most consistent associations observed among NHB and Hispanic individuals in lower-disadvantage neighborhoods, though these associations attenuated in several sensitivity analyses. In exploratory subgroup analyses, significant associations were not observed among individuals residing in the most disadvantaged neighborhoods, though these findings...

item.title: The cost of mentalizing: executive contributions to social cognition performance in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.description: BACKGROUND: Mentalizing deficits are common in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Performance at high-level socio-cognitive tasks may be particularly vulnerable to integrity of basic cognitive processes. However, the extent to which non-social functioning contributes to socio-cognitive impairment in ALS remains poorly understood. In this study, we addressed this question in a large cohort of patients.

item.title: Associated factors and cultivation strategies of positive social mentality among college students in the new era
item.description: CONCLUSION: Positive social mentality among medical students is associated with multiple interrelated environmental and relational factors rather than with gender or academic year. Targeted, multi-level interventions addressing these factors are needed to foster students' psychological well-being and civic engagement.

item.title: Editorial: Factors for the progression from latent tuberculosis infection to tuberculosis disease, volume II
item.description: No abstract

item.title: From fragmentation to integration: digital health as a catalyst for universal health coverage in Somalia
item.description: Universal Health Coverage (UHC) remains a major challenge in Somalia, where prolonged conflict, weak governance, fragmented service delivery, and donor dependence continue to undermine health system performance. Although digital health has emerged as a promising strategy for strengthening health systems, its implementation in Somalia has largely been characterized by fragmented, donor-driven, and disease-specific initiatives with limited integration into national health system reform. This...

item.title: Comparison of cardiopulmonary function in patients with scoliosis at rest and during exercise: a case-control study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Preoperative scoliosis is characterized by preserved resting indices but a frequently occult reduction in exercise reserve, including an exercise cardiac limitation revealed by O₂ pulse that resting echocardiography does not show. Thoracic height is a body-size-independent predictor of restrictive lung volume with a clinically usable threshold, while exercise reserve is multifactorial and requires direct CPET assessment. The two dimensions of preoperative cardiopulmonary risk should...

item.title: Preliminary analysis of the proportions and characteristics of dual TCR T cells and dual BCR B cells in echinococcus granulosus-infected mice using scRNA+TCR+BCR-seq
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Cystic echinococcosis (CE) is a zoonotic parasitic disease caused by Echinococcus granulosus, and the T and B cell responses and regulatory mechanisms in CE remain unclear.

item.title: Malignant potential of oral lichen planus without epithelial dysplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal studies
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The malignant transformation rate of OLP was very low, with a pooled estimate of 1.56%, supporting continued surveillance. Future research should focus on standardized diagnostic approaches and reliable risk stratification models to improve understanding of malignant transformation in OLP and ensure better population representation.

item.title: Irrigation fluid absorption induces metabolic and oxidative stress dysregulation activating NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways to drive hippocampal inflammatory responses
item.description: CONCLUSION: Excessive irrigation fluid absorption induces hippocampal neuroinflammation through metabolic disturbance and redox dysregulation, which activates NLRP3 and NF-κB pathways. These findings suggest potential therapeutic targets for preventing neurological complications during endoscopic procedures.

item.title: Type-, dose-, and subgroup-specific associations of dairy intake with depressive and anxiety symptoms among middle school students
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Dairy intake was differentially associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms among middle school students. More frequent milk and yogurt intake showed relatively consistent inverse associations with symptom scores, whereas associations for milk powder, cheese/cheese cubes, and amount-based dairy measures were less consistent and, for some measures, sensitive to model specification. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations and warrant further...

item.title: Editorial: Management of patients with dialysis dependent chronic kidney disease (DD-CKD)
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Social inequalities and the risk of multimorbidity in Mexican adults: an intersectional approach
item.description: CONCLUSION: This intersectional work reveals various social identities that are grouped into strata and represent patterns of social disadvantage associated with Multimorbidity.

item.title: Speech-based identification of suicide risk in patients with MDD: model development and 4-week follow-up validation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Speech-derived textual features showed potential value for supporting suicide risk identification in patients with MDD. Combining speech-derived textual information with clinical symptom measures may provide complementary information beyond standard symptom assessment. These findings suggest that speech-based approaches may support clinicians in identifying suicide risk among patients with MDD, although further validation in larger independent multicenter cohorts is needed before...

item.title: Disrupted valine metabolism and SCPC-mediated neurological toxicity in ECHS1 deficiency
item.description: CONCLUSION: These studies demonstrate that accumulation of ECHS1D-specific valine intermediates, particularly SCPC, contributes to mitochondrial dysfunction and disease severity in ECHS1D. Dietary valine modulation during adolescence showed limited therapeutic benefit and induced broader metabolic perturbations, underscoring the need for improved therapeutic strategies.

item.title: Early differentiation of viral encephalitis and autoimmune encephalitis by clinical and basic laboratory data
item.description: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Timely differentiation between autoimmune and viral causes of encephalitis is critical for guiding disease-specific treatment. This study aimed to develop a scoring system to facilitate early (< 6 h after presentation) differentiation between viral encephalitis (VE) and autoimmune encephalitis (AE).

item.title: Case Report: Favorable long-term outcomes of autologous PRF-augmented delayed replantation for traumatic avulsion of three mandibular anterior teeth with 10-year follow-up
item.description: The first-line treatment for permanent tooth avulsion is immediate replantation. Delayed replantation is associated with a high risk of survival-related complications, such as root resorption. Autologous platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) may promote the periodontal healing of delayed-replanted avulsed teeth and may potentially reduce the occurrence and progression of early root resorption. This case report explores the dental treatment process of autologous PRF-assisted delayed replantation in an adult...

item.title: CEST MRI Z-Spectra Reconstruction Using Transformer-based Deep Learning Models and Under Sampled Spectrum Signatures
item.description: Chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) contrast MRI provides unique molecular contrast by probing proton exchange between solutes and bulk water, but its clinical translation is limited by long acquisition times required to acquire finely sampled Z-spectra bringing a tradeoff between acquisition time and frequency offset responses. In this preliminary study, we investigated the performance of transformer-based deep learning models to reconstruct fully sampled CEST spectra. We first...

item.title: Neurobehavioral dysregulation, depressive symptoms, and cognition in former American football players
item.description: Neurobehavioral dysregulation (NBD) is a core clinical feature of traumatic encephalopathy syndrome (TES), but its relationships with repetitive head impact (RHI) exposure, cognitive performance, and depressive symptoms remain unclear. This study examined clinical factors associated with NBD among former American football players with substantial RHI exposure. Cross-sectional baseline data were analyzed from 179 former American football players enrolled in the DIAGNOSE CTE Research Project,...

item.title: The burden of disease among Canadian children across age groups between 1990 and 2023
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Child mortality and morbidity have been reduced since 1990 for children <5 years; among older age groups, mortality has been reduced, but morbidity levels are similar or higher. Causes differ, but sustained action across the paediatric mortality and morbidity spectrum is needed to accelerate improvements.

item.title: Age-related cardiac dysfunction is not associated with shorter telomere length in laboratory rats
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Ageing is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). Preclinical models of ageing are needed to better understand human diseases. Telomere shortening is a critical process in cellular ageing and senescence. In humans, it is well-established that telomere shortening in circulating leukocytes is associated with CVD, however, whether this applies to common preclinical models remains disputable. We investigated leukocyte telomere length (LTL), cardiac telomere length...

item.title: Preliminary Study on Stromal Nodule Detection Using B-Mode Ultrasound Images and Deep Learning
item.description: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a common condition among aging men. Currently, transrectal ultrasonography (TRUS) is used for detecting BPH but frequently falls short in accuracy. In this study, we investigated the use of a deep learning network for stromal nodule detection in prostate specimens exhibiting BPH using B-mode ultrasound (US) imaging. B-mode US data was captured from ex-vivo prostate specimens of human patients. Expert annotations differentiating between stromal and...

item.title: Association of NT-proBNP with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in elderly men with normal BMI and incident heart failure
item.description: CONCLUSION: NT-proBNP levels were higher in patients without lean NAFLD than in those with lean NAFLD. The coexistence of lean NAFLD and NT-proBNP > 8330 pg/mL was associated with increased all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in elderly normal-BMI men with incident HF.

item.title: Design and evaluation of a deformable multi-organ abdominal phantom for multimodality imaging applications
item.description: A deformable multi-organ abdominal phantom can have many applications in medical imaging and image-guided interventions. It can provide ground truth data for registration evaluation and procedure training. In this study, we designed and fabricated a deformable abdominal phantom for multimodal imaging applications. Computed tomography (CT) images of a human patient were used to segment the abdominal surface, kidneys, spleen, and liver. Scaled down 3D-printed molds were created based on the...

item.title: Patient classification in episodic migraine based on data-driven pain curve dynamics
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that the way migraine pain evolves over time may help identify clinically distinct patient profiles. Considering pain trajectory adds a dynamic dimension to migraine phenotyping that is not captured by traditional diagnostic criteria and may contribute to improved phenotyping and hypothesis generation for personalized therapeutic strategies. Further studies in larger cohorts are needed to clarify its potential clinical relevance.

item.title: Comparison of the efficacy of neuromodulation techniques based on corticospinal excitability in improving exercise-induced fatigue in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: TEAS combined with acupuncture may be associated with the most favorable SUCRA ranking, but this should be interpreted as exploratory for improving EIF in athletes. However, the overall quality of current evidence is low, and SUCRA rankings should be interpreted as exploratory. Future high-quality RCTs are needed to validate these findings and determine the optimal stimulation parameter ranges.

item.title: GlycoRNA-related cellular program scoring identifies Siglec- and myeloid-associated tumor microenvironments for glycoRNA validation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study presents an expression-based map of glycoRNA-related cellular program across human cancers. The results suggest that glycoRNA-related transcriptional programs tend to occur in immune- and myeloid-enriched tumor microenvironments, particularly those involving Siglec-associated features. These findings prioritize tumor contexts for biochemical, imaging, spatial, and perturbation-based glycoRNA validation.

item.title: Effect of bacteriophages on cytokine production by human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and their subpopulations
item.description: CONCLUSION: These results improve our understanding of phage-human immune system interactions, which is important for appreciating their broader impact on human homeostasis and for assessing the safety of phage therapy.

item.title: Coordinated cell division and growth drive meristem notch formation in Ceratopteris gametophytes
item.description: Meristems drive organogenesis and shape plant body plans, yet their morphology and cellular organization vary widely across land plants. Fern gametophytes develop a multicellular meristem that initiates at one flat margin of the prothallus and progressively forms a distinctive concave notch, producing the characteristic cordate gametophyte. Despite its importance for gametophyte growth and sexual organ formation, the cellular basis of meristem notch morphogenesis remains unclear. Here, we...

item.title: Suppressing the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway rescues pink1 deficiency in Drosophila and influences mitochondrial morphology
item.description: Sterol-regulatory element binding proteins (SREBP) are master transcriptional factors controlling lipogenesis. In Drosophila, the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway is essential for development. Homozygous SREBP mutants are lipid deficient and larval lethal, whereas excessive lipids in flies are often associated with neurodegeneration. Since SREBP has previously been identified as a risk factor for Parkinson's disease, we further investigated the role of SREBP-mediated lipogenesis in a pink1...

item.title: Low ambient temperatures regulate Arabidopsis abscisic acid signaling and seed germination via CBFs-ABI3/ABI5-ICE1 interactions
item.description: Seed germination is profoundly influenced by diverse environmental stimuli (e.g., temperatures), but the associated underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely uncharacterized. In this study, we demonstrated that low ambient temperatures, such as 16°C, suppress Arabidopsis thaliana seed germination, with endogenous abscisic acid (ABA) signaling revealed as a critical part of the underlying mechanism. The germination suppression and ABA response regulation by low ambient temperatures require...

item.title: Promoter variation in BraHDAC1 modulates stomatal regulation and thermotolerance in Brassica rapa
item.description: Heat stress severely limits the productivity of Brassica rapa, a key vegetable crop worldwide. Deciphering the genetic basis of thermotolerance is essential for developing climate-resilient cultivars. By integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with bulked segregant analysis (BSA), we identified two single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP1 and SNP2) in the promoter of the histone deacetylase gene BraHDAC1, which underlies natural variation in heat tolerance. These SNPs create a functional...

item.title: Electromigration-Biased Carbon Transport and Isotope Fractionation in High-Carbon-Solubility Metals
item.description: Electromigration, usually studied as a failure mechanism can also guide materials formation. We demonstrate that direct current drives interstitial carbon transport in solid cobalt and nickel leading to graphite precipitation, isotope fractionation, and distinct thermal properties of the recovered phase. Carbon supplied centrally accumulates as graphite 8-10 mm away on the cathode side, whereas alternating-current control experiments under comparable heating produce only thin deposits near the...

item.title: Integrating Traditional Persian Medicine With Quantum Biology: Towards a New Model in Personalised and Preventive Healthcare
item.description: RATIONALE, AIMS, AND OBJECTIVES: Traditional Persian Medicine (TPM) offers a holistic framework centered on humoral balance and individualized constitution (mizaj), yet it lacks formal mechanistic alignment with modern biophysical sciences. This paper explores the conceptual and mathematical integration of TPM with quantum biology to lay the foundation for an evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic model in personalized healthcare.

item.title: Industry updates in advanced therapy medicinal products and regenerative medicine - May 2026
item.description: Latest developments in the field of Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products and regenerative medicine compiled from publicly available information and press releases from non-academic institutions in May 2026.

item.title: Industry updates in advanced therapy medicinal products and regenerative medicine - April 2026
item.description: Latest developments in the field of Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products and regenerative medicine compiled from publicly available information and press releases from non-academic institutions in April 2026.

item.title: Discovery of potent anti-inflammatory flavonoid-sesquiterpenoid hybrids from Syzygium simile: Structure-activity relationships and nanomolar inhibition of human neutrophil activation
item.description: CONTEXT: Current anti-inflammatory drugs often cause significant adverse effects, underscoring the need for safer alternatives. Natural products with rare and distinctive scaffolds represent a promising source of leads for discovering new anti-inflammatory agents.

item.title: IgG78-Engineered Macrophage Membrane Biomimetic Nanoparticles for Synergistic Targeted Photothermal-Chemotherapy of Rheumatoid Arthritis
item.description: Clinical management of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) primarily involves non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), glucocorticoids, disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs), and biological agents or gene therapy; however, these treatments have notable limitations. DMARDs, particularly methotrexate (MTX), continue to be the cornerstone of first-line therapy, despite systemic side effects that restrict long-term application and heighten the treatment burden. This study identified elevated...

item.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C<sub>4</sub> Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework
item.description: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C(4) grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this...

item.title: Supraoptimal Mycorrhizal Colonisation Elicits Defence and Depletes Rhizosphere Inhabiting Massilia in Mild Salt‑Stressed Maize: A Split‑Root Comparison of Locally Colonised Roots
item.description: Environmental conditions, such as light availability, affect the growth‑promoting effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis. However, how the root‑rhizosphere continuum responds when mycorrhizal structures become unsuitable due to environmental deterioration remains unresolved. Using a split‑root system under mild salinity and low light, we generated two AM colonisation states (moderate and supraoptimal) and focused on roots with similar colonisation rates to compare local responses under...

item.title: Chronic Stress Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression via α5-nAChR/FOXM1 Signaling Pathway
item.description: The α5-nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α5-nAChR) mediates chronic stress-induced lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression. Forkhead Box M1 (FOXM1) is an oxidative stress-associated protein that is strongly associated with chronic stress and functions as a cancer-promoting transcription factor critical to LUAD. Our gene expression profiling demonstrated that CHRNA5 (encoding α5-nAChR) knockdown suppresses FOXM1 levels. It remains unknown whether and how α5-nAChR interacts with FOXM1 to promote...

item.title: Type IV-Dominated Plasmid-Encoded CRISPR-Cas Systems Are Enriched in Multireplicon and Multi-Stressor Resistance Plasmids Across the Global Plasmidome
item.description: Plasmids are central vectors of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). However, the features that distinguish the most epidemiologically successful resistance plasmids remain incompletely understood. CRISPR-Cas systems are classically regarded as barriers to horizontal gene transfer, which makes their occurrence within resistance plasmids yet unexplored at large scale. Here we analyzed 72,555 curated plasmid sequences from the Plasmid database (PLSDB) to test whether plasmid-encoded CRISPR-Cas systems...

item.title: MICA Allelic Variation Modulates Secretion and Protein Flexibility, Impacting on NKG2D-Mediated Immune Responses and Antibody Detection
item.description: NKG2D is an essential receptor for cancer immunosurveillance, activating Natural Killer (NK) and CD8^(+) T-cells to eliminate transformed cells. However, release of its ligands promotes immune evasion. Although new therapeutic strategies aim to block NKG2D-ligand shedding, the impact of allelic polymorphism on secretion mechanisms, either as soluble proteins or within extracellular vesicles (EVs), remains insufficiently explored. The glycosyl-phosphatidyl-inositol (GPI)-anchored MICA (MHC class...

item.title: Generating and Expanding Conventional Type 1 Dendritic Cells
item.description: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s) are specialized antigen-presenting cells that play essential roles in cross-presentation, immunity to intracellular pathogens, and antitumor immune responses. Their low abundance and limited accessibility in blood and many tissues have driven extensive efforts to generate and expand cDC1s for mechanistic and translational studies. Over the past two decades, advances in cDC1 biology have transformed the field from heterogeneous bone marrow-derived...

item.title: Time, Trust and Participation: A Nationwide Quantitative Study of Person-Centred Care in Forensic Mental Health Settings
item.description: Person-centred care emphasises the uniqueness of individuals through partnerships, the co-creation of care plans and coordinated health care. Its implementation in forensic mental health services is challenged by legal coercion and restrictive practices. Person-centred principles are embedded in legislation; however, national data on patients' perspectives on person-centred care are lacking. This study aimed to map person-centred care as perceived by patients and to identify areas for...

item.title: Prophylactic Soraphen A Treatment Attenuates Western Diet-Exacerbated IMQ-Induced Psoriasiform Inflammation
item.description: Psoriasis is a T-cell-mediated inflammatory disease amplified by metabolic stress. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 (ACC1)-dependent fatty acid synthesis is required for IL-17-producing T cells. Here, we asked whether short-term systemic administration of soraphen A (SorA), a dual ACC1/2 inhibitor, modulates imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasiform inflammation under normal diet (ND) and Western diet (WD) conditions. Female C57BL/6J mice were fed ND or WD for 12 weeks prior to daily intraperitoneal...

item.title: Geometric Descriptors Reveal Social Niche Dynamics in Japanese Macaques
item.description: Quantifying how group living shapes resource use requires linking within-group differentiation to between-group segregation, but existing isotopic niche metrics rarely capture both within a single geometric framework. We present two descriptors of multivariate isotopic niche structure: individual Mahalanobis distances (D(i)), measuring within-group peripherality, and a directional containment index (Asym), measuring how niche regions of coexisting groups are nested. We applied these metrics to...

item.title: Integrating environmental adaptation, breeding, and rhizobia bioinoculants for soybean expansion in Europe
item.description: Europe's heavy dependence on imported protein is environmentally and strategically costly. Soybean (Glycine max) offers a great opportunity to close this gap. Soybean cultivation can reduce reliance on synthetic nitrogen (N) fertiliser through its symbiosis with N-fixing bacteria (rhizobia). Nevertheless, it remains a relatively new crop across much of Europe and establishing it in the continent's diverse environments raises challenges of climate adaptation, symbiotic N fixation, and crop...

item.title: Chromatic and Morphological Determinants of Nipple-Areola Complex Attractiveness in Caucasian European Women
item.description: Both aesthetic and cancer-related surgery may affect the nipple-areola complex (NAC). The role of its color in aesthetic perception remains poorly understood. Given parallels with facial and genital skin, the aim of the study was to evaluate the contribution of chromatic properties, particularly vasculature-dependent skin redness, to the aesthetic perception of NAC. Standardized NAC images from 1,907 female photomodels were analyzed for morphologic and chromatic values. NAC redness was...

item.title: Integrated Spatial Multi-Omics Reveals Metabolic Hotspots of Paclitaxel Biosynthesis in Taxus yunnanensis
item.description: Paclitaxel (Taxol) is a broad-spectrum anticancer drug, but its clinical application is limited by insufficient production and supply. Although previous studies have noted regional differences in paclitaxel metabolism within stem tissues, the spatial compartmentalization characteristics remain unclear due to the lack of effective analytical methods. Here, we first profiled stem segments of a single Taxus yunnanensis stem spanning six longitudinal positions from juvenile (P1) to mature (P6)...

item.title: Copper Surface Engineering Enables Uniform Zn Plating in Zn Batteries at Unity N/P Ratio
item.description: Zinc (Zn) metal plating is notoriously sensitive to interfacial inefficiencies under Zn-limited conditions, where small losses of active Zn rapidly lead to premature cell failure. Here, we demonstrate a surface reconstruction strategy for copper (Cu) current collectors that enables exceptional performance at a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.0. By chemically etching Cu to create a sacrificial cuprous chloride (γ-CuCl) interface, we obtained a micro-textured Cu substrate with...

item.title: Does smartphone addiction exist? A critical evaluation of the validity of behavioural addiction symptoms in problematic smartphone use
item.description: BACKGROUND: The current debate raises the question of whether "smartphone addiction" really exists and whether the phenomenon can be considered as a distinct, clinically relevant disorder. This question is examined from three perspectives: 1) the terminology and definition of the problematic behaviour, 2) the evidence of clinical relevance, the theoretical embedding and empirical robustness of negative consequences and related psychological mechanisms, and 3) a critical reflection of current...

item.title: Integrative single-cell transcriptomic and metabolic profiling reveals lactate-driven glycolytic reprogramming and histone lactylation in colorectal cancer liver metastasis
item.description: Metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion are hallmarks of cancer metastasis, but how tumor metabolism shapes the immune microenvironment during colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains poorly understood. The role of E-cadherin (CDH1) beyond cell adhesion is unexplored. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime trajectory inference, and in vivo/in vitro functional assays in primary and liver-metastatic CRC models. CellChat was used to map intercellular communication. Histone...

item.title: The preCDD Network as a Model for Academic Preclinical Cancer Drug Development in Germany
item.description: Over the past two decades, oncology has achieved remarkable progress, mainly due to the broad implementation of novel generation immunotherapies. Despite the majority of cancer cases nowadays being curable, a significant portion of cancers remains incurable, highlighting the ongoing gap between biological discoveries and clinically applicable therapies. Marked unmet needs for novel drugs are remaining; at the same time, drug development is nearly exclusively performed by the pharmaceutical...

item.title: Synthetic Strategy to Novel Highly Functionalized Furan Analogues Bearing Imidazole-Thiazole Hybrids: Structural Characterization, Nanoparticle Formulations, Antimicrobial Evaluation, Molecular Docking Studies, and Molecular Dynamic Simulations
item.description: This study reports design and synthesis of novel highly functionalized furan analogues bearing imidazole-thiazole hybrids with potential antimicrobial activity. The synthesized compounds were prepared and characterized using spectroscopic tools and elemental analyses. The antimicrobial activity of all the synthesized compounds was evaluated against a panel of bacterial strains vs ciprofloxacin as the positive control. The results revealed a highly structure- and strain-dependent profile....

item.title: Efficacy and safety of Lianhua Qingwen versus oseltamivir in children with influenza: a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, positive parallel-controlled study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: LHQW was non-inferior to oseltamivir in clinical recovery time and resulted in faster defervescence and greater improvement in cough and sore throat, with comparable safety.

item.title: Molecular analysis of matched PIN, prostate cancer, and adjacent normal prostate tissue reveals distinct transcriptional signatures and recurrent genomic alterations
item.description: Prostate intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) is a recognized precursor to prostate cancer (PCa) and shares many histological and molecular features with invasive disease. To clarify the relationship between PIN and PCa, we performed integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses on epithelial and stromal laser-capture microdissected samples in matched PIN (n = 121), PCa (n = 217), and adjacent normal (AN, n = 115) prostate tissue from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples across three...

item.title: Depth sets the recovery clock: evidence for a time-at-pressure effect in sea lions
item.description: All air-breathing marine vertebrates face the same fundamental trade-off: time spent foraging underwater must be offset by surface recovery between dives. For decades, the dominant view in diving physiology has been that post-dive duration (PDD) reflects the repayment of oxygen debt and clearance of carbon dioxide and lactate. Using more than 800 000 dives from five sea lion species across 18 colonies spanning tropical to subpolar waters, we quantified how PDD scales with dive depth and duration...

item.title: Climate state controls the strength of the latitudinal diversity gradient
item.description: The latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG)-a decline in taxonomic richness from the Equator to the poles-is a fundamental biogeographic pattern on Earth today, yet its primary regulators remain debated. Whereas many of the proposed climatic and environmental drivers covary with latitude in the present day, these variables have fluctuated substantially over millions of years. The fossil record therefore offers a unique perspective on the response of diversity and, by extension, the LDG, to global...

item.title: Genome Sequencing Outperforms Exome Sequencing in Formalin-Fixed Paraffin Embedded Tumors Leading to Improved Treatment Options
item.description: Precision oncology is based on comprehensive molecular characterization of a patient's tumor. This is mostly realized by next-generation sequencing panels or exome sequencing. Data on the value of genome sequencing from formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) material in a clinical setting is still scarce. In this pilot, we generated datasets of matched exome and genome sequencing of FFPE tumor samples from 15 cancer patients to benchmark quality metrics, clinical feasibility, and added value...

item.title: Time-to-Event Analysis of Clinical Milestones in the ALS Natural History Consortium Dataset
item.description: INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Study of clinical milestones, particularly intermediate events like loss of ambulation, in large amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) cohorts is limited. Here, we leverage the ALS Natural History Consortium dataset to evaluate the time-to-event for several outcomes and prognostic factors that predict risk.

item.title: PIH1D2 Loss-of-Function Directs Ciliary and Cell Cycle Defects Resulting in Left Isomerism With or Without Biliary Atresia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings establish PIH1D2 as a novel disease gene for left isomerism heterotaxy, with biliary atresia observed in one of the patients. Loss of PIH1D2 impairs ciliogenesis and cell cycle progression, providing a mechanistic link between ciliary defects and abnormal left-right patterning. These results expand the spectrum of cilia-related laterality disorders and identify PIH1D2 as a critical regulator of human development.

item.title: Prophylactic oral calcium-vitamin D3-magnesium supplementation reduced citrate-related reactions during peripheral blood stem cell collection in healthy donors: A randomized controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: Prophylactic oral calcium-vitamin D3-magnesium supplementation markedly reduced citrate-related reactions during PBSC collection in healthy donors and may represent a practical approach to improving donor safety.

item.title: A novel supergene regulates alternative dispersal morphs without variation in social organization in the ant Myrmecina nipponica
item.description: Polymorphisms in complex traits with discrete phenotypes are often underpinned by non-recombining complexes of co-adaptive genes, known as supergenes. In disparate lineages of ants, it is increasingly evident that supergenes are important in regulating intra-specific variation in social organization (number of reproductive queens in a colony). Variation in social organization in ants is often associated with variation in dispersal, with multiple-queen (polygynous) colony types exhibiting more...

item.title: Lean Management of Surgical Instruments in Multidisciplinary Collaboration: Practice Research With Multidimensional Evaluation of Cost and Quality
item.description: CONCLUSION: The multidisciplinary collaborative Lean Management model enables precise allocation of surgical instrument resources, effectively reduces operational costs and significantly enhances nursing work efficiency and instrument management quality. This approach aligns with the requirements for high-quality development in modern operating rooms.

item.title: MEK1/2 Signalling establishes an alloreactive effector T cell program through SMAD4 during cardiac allograft rejection
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: MEK1/2 signalling regulates T cell activation and effector phenotypes via SMAD4 nuclear translocation in heart transplant rejection. Therapeutic intervention targeting this pathway may contribute to alloimmune response regulation and improve transplant outcomes.

item.title: Towards precision microbiome medicine through ecological network balance
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Anatomically Defined Motor Phenotypes Reveal Dissociated Trajectories of Progression, Neurofilament Profiles, and Survival in ALS
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Anatomically defined motor phenotypes identify reproducible ALS trajectories with distinct clinical and neurofilament profiles. Early propagation provides an actionable risk marker of disease aggressiveness, while combined upper and lower motor neuron dysfunction or lower motor neuron predominance is prognostically unfavorable. These findings support integrating structured phenotyping into prognostic models and clinical trial stratification.

item.title: CSF and plasma lipid profiling predicts risk of cognitive impairment in cognitively unimpaired older adults
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Age-related cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD) are strongly influenced by lipid metabolism, yet how central and peripheral lipid profiles relate to disease risk before symptom onset remains unclear.

item.title: Implementation strategies and adjunctive interventions for HIV testing and linkage-to-care in the United States: a systematic review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: U.S. HIV testing and linkage-to-care initiatives rely on multi-component implementation strategies centered on training, workflow/site reconfiguration, and clinician-facing supports, while adjunctive interventions chiefly target recipient capability and motivation. The field would benefit from standardized outcome definitions and rigorous comparative evaluations that link discrete strategies and adjunctive interventions through hypothesized mechanisms to specific implementation...

item.title: Diagnostic evaluation of long-read nanopore sequencing for pediatric CNS tumors
item.description: Long-read nanopore sequencing enables methylation-based CNS tumor classification while providing additional genomic information within a single assay. However, its performance across molecular features relevant to pediatric CNS tumor diagnostics and across available methylation classifiers remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated nanopore sequencing for integrated molecular characterization of pediatric CNS tumors and compared with data from DNA methylation arrays and Illumina short-read...

item.title: Breaking the Silence: A Mixed Methods Analysis Unveiling Barriers to Mental Health Service Use in Breast Cancer Survivors With Clinically Significant Distress
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Few clinically distressed breast cancer survivors utilize MHS. Anxiety, depression, and PTS symptoms may better predict MHS use than FCR, potentially due to avoidant coping among fearful survivors. Interventions targeting avoidance, alongside survivor-informed improvements in mental health care delivery, may enhance MHS access and outcomes.

item.title: Plasma β-synuclein associates with hippocampal synaptic density measured with [<sup>11</sup>C]UCB-J PET and plasma tau markers in Alzheimer's disease
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Plasma β-synuclein is a promising blood-based synaptic biomarker, but relationships with synaptic density as indicated by [^(11)C]UCB-J positron emission tomography (PET), and blood biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, neurodegeneration, and astrocyte activation need further characterization.

item.title: Diffuse large B cell lymphoma in rheumatoid arthritis express polyreactive and autoreactive BCRs binding protein modifications
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The data suggest a possible link between polyreactivity and anti-MDA/MAA autoreactivity in RA-DLBCL lymphomagenesis. We hypothesize that high inflammation burden could increase antigen load which may trigger polyreactive and modified-protein B cell responses and/or maintain lymphoma cell survival.

item.title: Can blind box buying be addictive?: Measurement and associations with gambling disorder among Chinese adults
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The current study is the first exploratory investigation of problematic blind box buying and its relationship with GD. It provides evidence for the validity and reliability of PBBS for measuring problematic blind box buying. Moreover, its findings also support the addictive potential of blind box buying and the associated risk with gambling disorder. These findings provide practical insights for the regulation and policy of blind box commerce and GD intervention.

item.title: Adult ADHD, PARK2 copy number variations and the blood-brain barrier: Culture duration-dependent metabolic alterations in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived in vitro models
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged culture was associated with broad, ADHD- and PARK2 genotype-independent metabolic remodeling, whereas mitochondrial and metabolic alterations associated with ADHD and PARK2 CNVs were overall small. This study identifies culture duration as a critical parameter for the characterization of hiPSC-derived BBB in vitro models and supports the feasibility of using donor-specific BCECs at the end of differentiation to investigate BBB-associated mechanisms in adult ADHD and PARK2...

item.title: Piezo1-mitochondrial calcium uniporter coupling-dependent mechanotransduction basis for acupuncture to drive analgesia
item.description: CONCLUSION: Piezo1 acts as a core peripheral mechanotransducer that converts local mechanical stimuli generated by acupuncture into downstream analgesic signaling in CFA-induced inflammatory pain. This study delineates a specific myocyte-originated mechanotransduction axis underlying acupuncture analgesia under inflammatory conditions, thereby providing mechanistic insights for understanding acupoint-specific therapeutic effects.

item.title: PEDF alleviates autoimmune uveitis and reprograms Treg metabolism
item.description: T cell-mediated autoimmune diseases remain difficult to manage owing to limited options and adverse effects of current immunosuppressants; safer, tolerance-preserving approaches are needed. We identify pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) as an endogenous regulator of ocular immunity with therapeutic potential. PEDF expression was induced during autoimmune uveitis (AU) in patients and during experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU) progression, suggesting an endogenous compensatory response to...

item.title: Quercetin attenuates maternal respiratory virus-induced fetal neuroimmune dysregulation
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings identify maternal NK cell-derived granzyme B as a central driver of respiratory virus-induced fetal neuroimmune disturbance and support quercetin as a dual-action immunomodulatory candidate capable of mitigating maternal immune dysregulation and fetal neuroinflammation.

item.title: Comparative proteomics of human anterior lens capsules reveals ATP6V1A-associated lysosomal dysregulation in age-related cataract with primary angle-closure glaucoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PACG-associated ALCs show a distinct molecular signature characterized by impaired proteostasis and ATP6V1A-associated lysosomal dysregulation. These findings identify ATP6V1A-associated lysosomal dysfunction as a candidate molecular link between elevated IOP, lens epithelial injury, and the coexistence of PACG and ARC.

item.title: Hydroxychloroquine suppresses replication of PRRSV via dual regulation of autophagic flux and NF-κB-driven inflammatory signaling
item.description: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) induces excessive autophagy and aberrant nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cell (NF-κB) hyperactivation, triggering severe respiratory and reproductive disorders in pigs and causing massive economic losses to the global swine industry. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate (HCQ), a classic autophagy inhibitor, restricts PRRSV proliferation in vitro; however, its in vivo protective efficacy and dual-targeted molecular...

item.title: The role of BDNF, CREB, DAT, GFAP and Arc in manic- and OCD-like behavioral phenotypes in both sexes of rats exposed to REM sleep deprivation
item.description: Rapid-eye movement sleep deprivation (REM SD) has controversial effects on behavioral functions and cognitive abilities. Recent evidence has shown that REM SD in rats may lead to manic- and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)-like behaviors. The present study aimed to assess the effect of REM SD in both sexes of rats on locomotor activity, anxiety-like behavior, stereotyped behaviors, and OCD-like behavior. The possible role of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), cAMP response...

item.title: The RNA-binding protein KHSRP drives prostate cancer progression through a DUSP6 dependent axis
item.description: CONCLUSION: KHSRP drives PCa progression through a DUSP6-dependent signaling axis by repressing DUSP6 at the post-transcriptional level and facilitating coordinated activation of ERK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. These findings identify a previously unrecognized KHSRP-DUSP6 regulatory axis in PCa and suggest that KHSRP may serve as a potential therapeutic target.

item.title: BTBD9-driven IMPDH2 ubiquitination governs sleep homeostasis by gating adenosine metabolism in the basal forebrain
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway that links human genetic risk to basal forebrain control of sleep homeostasis. By defining BTBD9 as a molecular regulator of purine metabolism, this study provides a mechanistic framework for understanding and potentially targeting BTBD9-related sleep dysregulation.

item.title: Tracing-based drawing method enhances anatomy learning outcomes and proportional awareness: a randomized cross-over study
item.description: CONCLUSION: TBDM was associated with higher drawing performance and more positive learner ratings than TMBM. A positive method contrast was observed at both the immediate and one-week delayed assessments, although the difference was smaller at the delayed assessment. TBDM may provide a low-cost, structured complement to existing anatomy-learning methods. Its longer-term and transferable educational effects require further investigation.

item.title: Today's flow, tomorrow's subjective well-being: temporal dynamics in the Chinese educational context
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the temporal precedence of academic flow in predicting daily subjective well-being, consistent with a eudaimonic perspective on student development. In practice, these results encourage educators and institutional practitioners to prioritize cultivating optimal learning experiences as a meaningful strategy to sustain student well-being in higher education.

item.title: Association of tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA dynamics with radiologic disease assessment in a single-center real-world sarcoma cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Tumor-informed ctDNA monitoring was feasible in 70% of screened patients and showed high concordance with radiologic disease assessment in this real-world sarcoma cohort. These findings support prospective evaluation of ctDNA as an adjunct to imaging for longitudinal disease monitoring in patients with a suitable tumor-informed target, while broader tumor-informed approaches may be required for patients whose tumors are not adequately covered by predefined targeted panels.

item.title: Preliminary Investigation of Maternal and Offspring Genetic Effects of the DBH Gene in Probands with Schizophrenia and Their Relatives
item.description: CONCLUSION: This pilot study suggests a potential maternal genetic effect of DBH rs5320 in schizophrenia. However, these preliminary findings require validation in larger and more complete family-based samples.

item.title: Desoxo-narchinol A and water extract of Nardostachys jatamansi ameliorate house dust mite-induced atopic dermatitis by regulating Nrf2/HO-1 signaling
item.description: Nardostachys jatamansi has traditionally been used to treat gastrointestinal disorders. Although it was recently reported to have anti-inflammatory properties, the pharmacological potential of water extract of Nardostachys jatamansi (WENJ) against atopic dermatitis (AD)-like skin inflammation remains unclear. We investigated the effects of WENJ on a house dust mite-induced AD-like mouse model by assessing phenotypic severity, histopathological changes, and cytokine expression. Transcriptomic...

item.title: Updated guide to the assessment of mammalian cellular senescence
item.description: Cellular senescence is a stable cell cycle arrest, which has a crucial role in organismal aging and many chronic diseases. Here, we present an updated MiniResource that extends the methods for mammalian senescence assays, including analyses of cell cycle arrest and cellular morphology, changes in transcriptomic signatures, and fluorescence-based tools. This work will provide practical guidance to help researchers design appropriate experiments for assessing cellular senescence.

item.title: In Vitro Human Arteriole Microphysiological System with Physiological Scale and Functional Vasoactivity Enabled by a Dual Material Fabrication Strategy
item.description: Arterioles are the principal regulators of vascular tone, yet their small size and deep tissue location hinder direct investigation of their roles in microvascular disease. To address this, we developed a human microphysiological arteriole distinguished from previous models by simultaneously integrating an arteriole-scale caliber (~200 μm), continuous perfusion culture, and active vasoactivity. The vessel autonomously forms and matures under flow through a spatially regulated coating strategy...

item.title: Corrosion-driven interfacial reconstruction enables selective two-carbon ethanol oxidation at industrial current density
item.description: The sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) severely limit the energy efficiency of conventional water electrolysis. Replacing OER with thermodynamically favorable small-molecule oxidation offers a promising strategy to reduce energy consumption while enabling value-added chemical production. Here, we report a corrosion-driven interfacial reconstruction strategy to in situ construct a self-supported nickel-iron layered double hydroxide/iron oxyhydroxide (NiFe-LDH/FeOOH)...

item.title: Polarity-Selective Engineering of In-Gap States in Amorphous Silicon Nitride via Distinct Structural and Electronic Origins
item.description: Precise control of trap states in amorphous dielectrics requires identifying the fundamentally different physical origins of hole and electron trapping. Here, in amorphous silicon nitride (a‑SiN(x)), we demonstrate a dual-origin mechanism where the two trap polarities arise from decoupled structural and electronic mechanisms, enabling polarity-selective engineering of charge storage behavior. item.description: Vertical asymmetry in two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides induces intrinsic dipoles, symmetry-breaking functionalities, and interface-specific electronic reconstruction. However, existing Janus synthesis processes rely on sequential treatments, high-temperature substitution, or solid-phase precursors. item.title: Recognition-dependent activation of the Arabidopsis RRS1-R/RPS4 TIR-NLR immune receptor pair
item.description: Plant TIR domain-containing proteins exhibit NADase activity upon pathogen effector recognition, creating small molecules that activate defense via EDS1 and its associated proteins. Arabidopsis RPS4 and RRS1 comprise a TIR-NLR immune receptor pair that recognizes multiple effector proteins including AvrRps4 and PopP2. item.title: Adaptive Cellular Responsiveness to Electrical Stimulation at the Skin-Electrode Interface
item.description: Wearable electrical stimulation (ES) devices are emerging platforms for wound healing, where cellular responses at the skin-electrode interface critically influence therapeutic outcomes. Here, we demonstrate that skin cells dynamically adapt to sustained ES by upregulating voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs) and enhancing their sensitivity to electrical cues. item.title: Surface-Selective Pt Enrichment for Stabilizing Ultrathin 2D PtCu Nanosheets Toward Durable Oxygen Reduction
item.description: Ultrathin Pt-based 2D alloy nanosheets are promising electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their high surface-to-volume ratios and favorable facet-dependent activity. However, their thermodynamic instability and susceptibility to transition metal dissolution present critical barriers to their practical application. item.title: Formation-Dependent Cardinality Concealment of Target Swarms in Multifunction Radar
item.description: Recognizing a swarm of unmanned surface vehicles does not guarantee that its physical cardinality can be recovered. This study examines how formation, viewing aspect ψ, defined as the orientation of the formation relative to the radar line of sight (RLOS), and sensing resources affect these two tasks in a multifunction radar. item.title: Nutrient Sensing, Monitoring, and Control for Hydroponic Crop Production in Smart Greenhouses
item.description: Hydroponic crop production in smart greenhouses requires accurate nutrient monitoring and reliable control, especially in recirculating systems. This review critically examines sensing principles, data acquisition, control strategies, actuation, feedback, and system integration. Electrical conductivity (EC) and pH are widely used for dosing, but EC cannot quantify individual nutrient concentrations. item.title: Development of a Wearable Torsion Sensor Utilizing a Geometric Model and a Hysteresis-Compensated Calibration Engine
item.description: Measuring torsional movement is crucial for tracking human kinematics in applications such as virtual reality, biomechanics, rehabilitation, and soft robotic joints.
